overview: The Marathon County Board of Supervisors held its annual budget meeting on November 10, 2026, taking up the 2027 budget and property tax levy along with several amendments. Key debates centered on a proposed $1.75 million reduction to the tax levy (defeated), and whether to continue funding Flock license plate reader cameras in the sheriff's department budget (ultimately moved to contingency pending policy review). The meeting drew a near-capacity crowd and reflected significant tension between fiscal conservatives seeking levy reductions and those defending the county's highway shop funding strategy.

discussions.item: Consent Agenda Items C8 through C13B
discussions.body: Supervisor Straub requested that item C13C be pulled for a separate vote. The remaining consent agenda items C8 through C13B were approved unanimously on a motion by Supervisor Dreybeck, seconded by Supervisor Joong.

discussions.item: C13C — Sale of Tax Deeded Property for $1 (Resolution 77-26)
discussions.body: Supervisor Straub objected to selling the property for $1, arguing it was worth $25,000–$45,000 and that the county could have demolished the mold-infested structure itself cheaply. Supervisor Robinson countered that a certified appraiser valued the property at zero due to severe mold contamination, that the city would demolish it and return it to housing stock, and that accepting the transfer relieved the county of remediation liability. The motion to approve the $1 sale passed but was not unanimous.

Supervisor Hoppa raised safety concerns about lighting on the bridge where ATVs and UTVs would share the road. The Highway Commissioner confirmed no additional county lighting was planned since it is a state road, and noted ATVs are required to have headlights and taillights when operating on roads. Supervisor Neiseth expressed concern about the 55 mph speed limit on the corridor but was told speed limits are state-controlled. Supervisor Mask encouraged support, citing constituents' safety concerns. The ordinance passed unanimously.

discussions.item: 2027 Budget — Amendment 5: $1.75 Million Tax Levy Reduction
discussions.body: Supervisor Sandelski moved to reduce the proposed tax levy increase by $1.75 million, funded by drawing from the highway fund rather than debt levy, arguing the county's 8% levy increase was 'egregious' and that highway fund reserves were healthy. County Administrator Leonard and Supervisor Robinson gave extensive rebuttals, explaining that the highway fund balance is nearly fully committed to the $55 million highway shop project and that the interfund loan strategy was the least costly approach. Supervisors Dickinson, Straub, and Cavelli spoke in favor of the amendment, while Vice Chair Boes and Robinson urged rejection given the Bug Tussle broadband financial liability also looming. Debate was closed by a two-thirds vote after Supervisor Krebs called the question. The amendment was defeated.

discussions.item: 2027 Budget — Amendment 1: Flock Camera Funding ($6,300 to HR Finance Contingency)
discussions.body: Supervisor Robinson moved to remove $6,300 for Flock license plate reader cameras from the Sheriff's Department hardware/software budget and place it in the HR Finance Committee contingency fund, pending policy discussions between Sheriff Billick and privacy advocate Mr. Gallo on data retention, access, and audit requirements. Supervisor Neiseth moved an amendment to instead eliminate the $6,300 entirely and reduce the tax levy, citing Fourth Amendment concerns and constituent opposition. That amendment to the amendment failed. Robinson's original amendment — moving funds to contingency — then passed, though not unanimously, with the understanding that policy discussions would occur at Public Safety and HR Finance committees before any funds are released.

publicComment: No formal public comment period was held at this meeting, though Supervisor Trapp read extensively from a Wausau Pilot and Review investigative article by Shereen Siewert (published November 3–4, 2026) reporting that 1,410 law enforcement agencies across 40 states can search Marathon County's Flock camera data, contradicting Sheriff Billick's earlier public statements. References were also made to testimony from a citizen named Mr. Gallo at the prior week's public hearing regarding privacy concerns over Flock cameras.
actionItems: Sheriff's Department Flock camera funding ($6,300) moved to HR Finance contingency pending policy review by Public Safety Committee and HR Finance Committee
Sheriff Billick and privacy advocate Mr. Gallo directed to meet and work toward policy agreement on Flock data retention, access, and audit requirements

HR Finance and Property Committee directed to continue working with Extension, Education, Economic Development Committee to procure a broker to sell Thomas Street and River Drive properties to help repay highway shop interfund loan
Board to revisit highway shop funding strategy annually following each audit to identify opportunities to shorten the interfund loan repayment period
Administration to monitor and report on Bug Tussle broadband financial obligations, including a known $347,000 shortfall due before July and a projected $1.5 million obligation the following year
ATV/UTV use on Highway 34 authorized under Ordinance 53-26 with required signage at route endpoints
Tax-deeded property (Parcel 291-2907-354-0252) authorized for sale to the city for $1 under Resolution 77-26
